permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always

jobs:
  platform:
    name: Portable checks (${{ matrix.os }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 25
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-26-intel, windows-latest]
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'
      - name: Install pinned native inspection toolchain
        run: python scripts/release/sevenzip.py install
      - name: Install frontend dependencies
        working-directory: frontend
        run: npm ci
      - name: Frontend static checks
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        working-directory: frontend
        run: |
          npm run format:check
          npm run lint
          npm run typecheck
      - name: Audit frontend dependencies
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        working-directory: frontend
        run: npx --yes audit-ci --config audit-ci.json

      - name: Validate public help and MCP
        run: |
          npm ci --prefix tools/help --ignore-scripts
          node --test tools/help/*.test.mjs

      - name: Audit help dependencies
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: npm audit --prefix tools/help --audit-level=high

      - name: Frontend unit tests and coverage
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        working-directory: frontend
        run: npm run test:coverage

      - name: Frontend unit tests (macOS and Windows)
        if: runner.os != 'Linux'
        working-directory: frontend
        run: npm test

      - name: Seal browser unit line map from this run
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: node scripts/ci/unit-coverage-artifact.mjs seal frontend/coverage/lcov.info target/ui-unit-coverage

      - name: Upload browser unit line map
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: ui-unit-coverage-${{ github.sha }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: target/ui-unit-coverage/
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

      - name: Upload frontend coverage
        if: always() && matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: frontend-coverage-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: frontend/coverage/
          if-no-files-found: warn

      - name: Delivery and AI eval smoke
        if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'
        run: |
          make eval-smoke
          node --test scripts/test-ai-eval.mjs

      - name: Install Rust for diagnostic Cargo fixtures
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - name: Native release inspection regression
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y nsis

      - name: Verify native NSIS payload equivalence
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: python scripts/release/test_native_nsis.py -v

      - name: Diagnostic and release gate regressions (all platforms)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          node scripts/check-repository-hygiene.mjs
          node --test scripts/diagnostics/*.test.mjs

      - name: Build retention safeguards (all platforms)
        run: python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p test_build_retention.py -v

      - name: Publish frontend coverage
        if: >-
          matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest' &&
          !(github.event_name == 'pull_request' &&
            github.base_ref == 'dev' &&
            github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'dependabot[bot]')
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@303a32d7a59b442fa8d48b6a1cc6825c09c847a5 # v7.1.1
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          files: frontend/coverage/lcov.info
          name: frontend-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          fail_ci_if_error: true

  source:
    name: Source and supply-chain checks
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1
      # Source/policy scanners have identical inputs on each OS; run them once.
      # Gitleaks owns the full-history secret scan in its independent workflow.
      - name: Install Rust
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: rustfmt
      - name: Rust formatting
        run: cargo fmt --all -- --check
      - name: Install source scanners
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2.88.1
        with:
          tool: cargo-deny,cargo-machete,typos-cli,shellcheck
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v7
        with:
          go-version: '1.25'
          cache: false
      - name: Install workflow scanner
        run: |
          go install github.com/rhysd/actionlint/cmd/actionlint@v1.7.12
          echo "$(go env GOPATH)/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      - name: Source and supply-chain policy
        run: |
          typos
          cargo deny check
          cargo machete
          shellcheck --severity=warning scripts/*.sh scripts/release/*.sh .claude/hooks/*.sh hooks/*
          actionlint

name: UI E2E

# Browser end-to-end tests for the React UI (Playwright + Chromium, headless). Drives the real
# app with a mocked Tauri IPC layer — guards the rendering/wiring that black-screened v0.1.0.
# The Rust multi-process backend E2E lives separately (`make e2e`).
on:
  merge_group:
    types: [checks_requested]
  push:
    branches: ["main", "dev"]
  pull_request:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 3 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      extended:
        description: Run extended theme, locale, resize and memory scenarios
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'merge_group' || github.event_name == 'push' }}

jobs:
  health:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/check-health.yml
    secrets: inherit

  linux:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/ui-shards.yml
    with:
      operating_systems: '["ubuntu-24.04"]'

  desktop:
    # Admit the desktop browser burst after portable unit/static checks finish.
    needs: health
    uses: ./.github/workflows/ui-shards.yml
    with:
      operating_systems: '["macos-latest","windows-latest"]'

  coverage:
    # This existing name is required by branch protection. It now certifies
    # successful shards plus their complete current-source coverage upload.
    name: Full Linux UI regression

          UNIT_COVERAGE: ${{ needs.health.result }}

name: Sanitizers

# Memory-safety / leak guardrail: runs the pure-Rust core test suite under
# AddressSanitizer (ASan, which embeds LeakSanitizer) so a genuine leak or
# use-after-free in the protocol core fails the build.
#
# Scope: ONLY `mesh-talk-core --lib` (the UI-free core). The Tauri app links
# GTK/WebKit C libraries whose internals trip ASan with false positives we can't
# fix from here, so the app is deliberately excluded.
#
# Run on PRs targeting main so branch protection can require this memory-safety
# check before merge. Run again on main so the README badge reflects the merged
# code; keep the weekly run to catch toolchain and dependency drift.
# ASan needs the nightly toolchain + `-Z build-std` (a full std rebuild).
on:
  merge_group:
    types: [checks_requested]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  push:

  schedule:

  contents: read

---
name: using-git-worktrees
description: Use when starting feature work that needs isolation from current workspace or before executing implementation plans - creates isolated git worktrees with smart directory selection and safety verification
---

# Using Git Worktrees

## Overview

Git worktrees create isolated workspaces sharing the same repository, allowing work on multiple branches simultaneously without switching.

**Core principle:** Systematic directory selection + safety verification = reliable isolation.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the using-git-worktrees skill to set up an isolated workspace."

## Directory Selection Process

Follow this priority order:

### 1. Check Existing Directories

```bash
# Check in priority order
ls -d .worktrees 2>/dev/null     # Preferred (hidden)
ls -d worktrees 2>/dev/null      # Alternative
```

**If found:** Use that directory. If both exist, `.worktrees` wins.

### 2. Check CLAUDE.md

```bash
grep -i "worktree.*director" CLAUDE.md 2>/dev/null
```

**If preference specified:** Use it without asking.

### 3. Ask User

If no directory exists and no CLAUDE.md preference:

```
No worktree directory found. Where should I create worktrees?

1. .worktrees/ (project-local, hidden)
2. ~/.config/superpowers/worktrees/<project-name>/ (global location)

Which would you prefer?
```

## Safety Verification

### For Project-Local Directories (.worktrees or worktrees)

**MUST verify directory is ignored before creating worktree:**

```bash
# Check if directory is ignored (respects local, global, and system gitignore)
git check-ignore -q .worktrees 2>/dev/null || git check-ignore -q worktrees 2>/dev/null
```

**If NOT ignored:**

Per Jesse's rule "Fix broken things immediately":
1. Add appropriate line to .gitignore
2. Commit the change
3. Proceed with worktree creation

**Why critical:** Prevents accidentally committing worktree contents to repository.

### For Global Directory (~/.config/superpowers/worktrees)

No .gitignore verification needed - outside project entirely.

## Creation Steps

### 1. Detect Project Name

```bash
project=$(basename "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)")
```

### 2. Create Worktree

```bash
# Determine full path
case $LOCATION in
  .worktrees|worktrees)
    path="$LOCATION/$BRANCH_NAME"
    ;;
  ~/.config/superpowers/worktrees/*)
    path="~/.config/superpowers/worktrees/$project/$BRANCH_NAME"
    ;;
esac

# Create worktree with new branch
git worktree add "$path" -b "$BRANCH_NAME"
cd "$path"
```

### 3. Run Project Setup

Auto-detect and run appropriate setup:

```bash
# Node.js
if [ -f package.json ]; then npm install; fi

# Rust
if [ -f Cargo.toml ]; then cargo build; fi

# Python
if [ -f requirements.txt ]; then pip install -r requirements.txt; fi
if [ -f pyproject.toml ]; then poetry install; fi

# Go
if [ -f go.mod ]; then go mod download; fi
```

### 4. Verify Clean Baseline

Run tests to ensure worktree starts clean:

```bash
# Examples - use project-appropriate command
npm test
cargo test
pytest
go test ./...
```

**If tests fail:** Report failures, ask whether to proceed or investigate.

**If tests pass:** Report ready.

### 5. Report Location

```
Worktree ready at <full-path>
Tests passing (<N> tests, 0 failures)
Ready to implement <feature-name>
```

## Quick Reference

| Situation | Action |
|-----------|--------|
| `.worktrees/` exists | Use it (verify ignored) |
| `worktrees/` exists | Use it (verify ignored) |
| Both exist | Use `.worktrees/` |
| Neither exists | Check CLAUDE.md → Ask user |
| Directory not ignored | Add to .gitignore + commit |
| Tests fail during baseline | Report failures + ask |
| No package.json/Cargo.toml | Skip dependency install |

## Common Mistakes

### Skipping ignore verification

- **Problem:** Worktree contents get tracked, pollute git status
- **Fix:** Always use `git check-ignore` before creating project-local worktree

### Assuming directory location

- **Problem:** Creates inconsistency, violates project conventions
- **Fix:** Follow priority: existing > CLAUDE.md > ask

### Proceeding with failing tests

- **Problem:** Can't distinguish new bugs from pre-existing issues
- **Fix:** Report failures, get explicit permission to proceed

### Hardcoding setup commands

- **Problem:** Breaks on projects using different tools
- **Fix:** Auto-detect from project files (package.json, etc.)

## Example Workflow

```
You: I'm using the using-git-worktrees skill to set up an isolated workspace.

[Check .worktrees/ - exists]
[Verify ignored - git check-ignore confirms .worktrees/ is ignored]
[Create worktree: git worktree add .worktrees/auth -b feature/auth]
[Run npm install]
[Run npm test - 47 passing]

Worktree ready at /Users/jesse/myproject/.worktrees/auth
Tests passing (47 tests, 0 failures)
Ready to implement auth feature
```

## Red Flags

**Never:**
- Create worktree without verifying it's ignored (project-local)
- Skip baseline test verification
- Proceed with failing tests without asking
- Assume directory location when ambiguous
- Skip CLAUDE.md check

**Always:**
- Follow directory priority: existing > CLAUDE.md > ask
- Verify directory is ignored for project-local
- Auto-detect and run project setup
- Verify clean test baseline

## Integration

**Called by:**
- **brainstorming** (Phase 4) - REQUIRED when design is approved and implementation follows
- **subagent-driven-development** - REQUIRED before executing any tasks
- **executing-plans** - REQUIRED before executing any tasks
- Any skill needing isolated workspace

**Pairs with:**
- **finishing-a-development-branch** - REQUIRED for cleanup after work complete
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Publish promptly after cheap checks; comprehensive validation runs in PR CI.
set -euo pipefail

repo_root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$repo_root"

preflight_args=()
full_preflight=0
separator=0
while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
    if [ "$1" = "--" ]; then
        separator=1
        shift
        break
    fi
    if [ "$1" = "--full-preflight" ]; then
        full_preflight=1
        shift
        continue
    fi
    preflight_args+=("$1")
    shift
done
if [ "$separator" -ne 1 ]; then
    echo "Usage: scripts/create-pr.sh [--full-preflight] [preflight selectors and UI specs] -- [gh pr create options]" >&2
    exit 2
fi
if [ -n "${GH_REPO:-}" ]; then
    echo "Unset GH_REPO: verified PR creation uses this checkout's repository." >&2
    exit 2
fi
for arg in "$@"; do
    case "$arg" in
        --head|--head=*|-H*|--repo|--repo=*|-R*|--base|--base=*|-B*)
            echo "Head/repository overrides are forbidden. Select the shared comparison/PR base before --." >&2
            exit 2
            ;;
    esac
done

# Bash 3.2 treats an empty array as unset under nounset.

# Using Git Worktrees

## Overview

Git worktrees create isolated workspaces sharing the same repository, allowing work on multiple branches simultaneously without switching.

**Core principle:** Systematic directory selection + safety verification = reliable isolation.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the using-git-worktrees skill to set up an isolated workspace."

## Directory Selection Process

Follow this priority order:

### 1. Check Existing Directories

```bash
# Check in priority order
ls -d .worktrees 2>/dev/null     # Preferred (hidden)
ls -d worktrees 2>/dev/null      # Alternative
```

**If found:** Use that directory. If both exist, `.worktrees` wins.

### 2. Check CLAUDE.md

```bash
grep -i "worktree.*director" CLAUDE.md 2>/dev/null
```

**If preference specified:** Use it without asking.

### 3. Ask User

If no directory exists and no CLAUDE.md preference:

```
No worktree directory found. Where should I create worktrees?

1. .worktrees/ (project-local, hidden)
2. ~/.config/superpowers/worktrees/<project-name>/ (global location)

Which would you prefer?
```

## Safety Verification

### For Project-Local Directories (.worktrees or worktrees)

**MUST verify directory is ignored before creating worktree:**

```bash
# Check if directory is ignored (respects local, global, and system gitignore)
git check-ignore -q .worktrees 2>/dev/null || git check-ignore -q worktrees 2>/dev/null
```

**If NOT ignored:**

Per Jesse's rule "Fix broken things immediately":
1. Add appropriate line to .gitignore
2. Commit the change
3. Proceed with worktree creation

**Why critical:** Prevents accidentally committing worktree contents to repository.

### For Global Directory (~/.config/superpowers/worktrees)

No .gitignore verification needed - outside project entirely.

## Creation Steps

### 1. Detect Project Name

```bash
project=$(basename "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)")
```

### 2. Create Worktree

```bash
# Determine full path
case $LOCATION in
  .worktrees|worktrees)
    path="$LOCATION/$BRANCH_NAME"
    ;;
  ~/.config/superpowers/worktrees/*)
    path="~/.config/superpowers/worktrees/$project/$BRANCH_NAME"
    ;;
esac

# Create worktree with new branch
git worktree add "$path" -b "$BRANCH_NAME"
cd "$path"
```

### 3. Run Project Setup

Auto-detect and run appropriate setup:

```bash
# Node.js
if [ -f package.json ]; then npm install; fi

# Rust
if [ -f Cargo.toml ]; then cargo build; fi

# Python
if [ -f requirements.txt ]; then pip install -r requirements.txt; fi
if [ -f pyproject.toml ]; then poetry install; fi

# Go
if [ -f go.mod ]; then go mod download; fi
```

### 4. Verify Clean Baseline

Run tests to ensure worktree starts clean:

```bash
# Examples - use project-appropriate command
npm test
cargo test
pytest
go test ./...
```

**If tests fail:** Report failures, ask whether to proceed or investigate.

**If tests pass:** Report ready.

### 5. Report Location

```
Worktree ready at <full-path>
Tests passing (<N> tests, 0 failures)
Ready to implement <feature-name>
```

## Quick Reference

| Situation | Action |
|-----------|--------|
| `.worktrees/` exists | Use it (verify ignored) |
| `worktrees/` exists | Use it (verify ignored) |
| Both exist | Use `.worktrees/` |
| Neither exists | Check CLAUDE.md → Ask user |
| Directory not ignored | Add to .gitignore + commit |
| Tests fail during baseline | Report failures + ask |
| No package.json/Cargo.toml | Skip dependency install |

## Common Mistakes

### Skipping ignore verification

- **Problem:** Worktree contents get tracked, pollute git status
- **Fix:** Always use `git check-ignore` before creating project-local worktree

### Assuming directory location

- **Problem:** Creates inconsistency, violates project conventions
- **Fix:** Follow priority: existing > CLAUDE.md > ask

### Proceeding with failing tests

- **Problem:** Can't distinguish new bugs from pre-existing issues
- **Fix:** Report failures, get explicit permission to proceed

### Hardcoding setup commands

- **Problem:** Breaks on projects using different tools
- **Fix:** Auto-detect from project files (package.json, etc.)

## Example Workflow

```
You: I'm using the using-git-worktrees skill to set up an isolated workspace.

[Check .worktrees/ - exists]
[Verify ignored - git check-ignore confirms .worktrees/ is ignored]
[Create worktree: git worktree add .worktrees/auth -b feature/auth]
[Run npm install]
[Run npm test - 47 passing]

Worktree ready at /Users/jesse/myproject/.worktrees/auth
Tests passing (47 tests, 0 failures)
Ready to implement auth feature
```

## Red Flags

**Never:**
- Create worktree without verifying it's ignored (project-local)
- Skip baseline test verification
- Proceed with failing tests without asking
- Assume directory location when ambiguous
- Skip CLAUDE.md check

**Always:**
- Follow directory priority: existing > CLAUDE.md > ask
- Verify directory is ignored for project-local
- Auto-detect and run project setup
- Verify clean test baseline

## Integration

**Called by:**
- **brainstorming** (Phase 4) - REQUIRED when design is approved and implementation follows
- **subagent-driven-development** - REQUIRED before executing any tasks
- **executing-plans** - REQUIRED before executing any tasks
- Any skill needing isolated workspace

**Pairs with:**
- **finishing-a-development-branch** - REQUIRED for cleanup after work complete

name: Sanitizers

# Memory-safety / leak guardrail: runs the pure-Rust core test suite under
# AddressSanitizer (ASan, which embeds LeakSanitizer) so a genuine leak or
# use-after-free in the protocol core fails the build.
#
# Scope: ONLY `mesh-talk-core --lib` (the UI-free core). The Tauri app links
# GTK/WebKit C libraries whose internals trip ASan with false positives we can't
# fix from here, so the app is deliberately excluded.
#
# Run on PRs targeting main so branch protection can require this memory-safety
# check before merge. Run again on main so the README badge reflects the merged
# code; keep the weekly run to catch toolchain and dependency drift.
# ASan needs the nightly toolchain + `-Z build-std` (a full std rebuild).
on:
  merge_group:
    types: [checks_requested]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  push:
    branches: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 6 * * 1" # Mondays 06:00 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:

# Read-only: just checks out and runs the test suite under the sanitizer.
permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'merge_group' }}

jobs:
  cohort:
    name: Resolve ASan nightly cohort
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      toolchain: ${{ steps.cohort.outputs.toolchain }}
      rustc: ${{ steps.cohort.outputs.rustc }}
      cargo: ${{ steps.cohort.outputs.cargo }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - name: Resolve installed nightly manifest
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@nightly
        with:
          components: rust-src
      - name: Publish exact installed nightly cohort
        id: cohort
        run: node scripts/ci/asan.mjs cohort

  shards:
    name: ASan core shard (${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    needs: cohort
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:

name: UI E2E

  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:

        description: Run extended theme, locale, resize and memory scenarios

permissions:
  contents: read

  shards:

        shard: [1, 2, 3, 4]

      MESH_ASAN_RUSTC: ${{ needs.cohort.outputs.rustc }}
      MESH_ASAN_CARGO: ${{ needs.cohort.outputs.cargo }}
      RUSTFLAGS: "-Zsanitizer=address"
      RUSTDOCFLAGS: "-Zsanitizer=address"
      ASAN_OPTIONS: "detect_leaks=1"
      # Keep production case budgets and one instrumented test per runner.
      RUST_TEST_THREADS: "1"
    steps:
      - name: Checkout

      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0

          node-version: 22
      - name: Prepare hosted Linux build storage

      RUSTFLAGS: "-Zsanitizer=address"
      RUSTDOCFLAGS: "-Zsanitizer=address"
      ASAN_OPTIONS: "detect_leaks=1"
      RUST_TEST_THREADS: "1"
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - name: Download this attempt's ASan evidence
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: asan-${{ github.sha }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}-shard-*
          path: tmp/asan-union
      - name: Verify every actual shard and complete exact-source union
        run: node scripts/ci/asan.mjs verify tmp/asan-union
          !(github.event_name == 'pull_request' &&
            github.base_ref == 'dev' &&
            github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'dependabot[bot]')
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@303a32d7a59b442fa8d48b6a1cc6825c09c847a5 # v7.1.1
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          files: frontend/coverage/lcov.info
          name: frontend-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          fail_ci_if_error: true

  source:
    name: Source and supply-chain checks
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1
      # Source/policy scanners have identical inputs on each OS; run them once.
      # Gitleaks owns the full-history secret scan in its independent workflow.
      - name: Install Rust
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: rustfmt
      - name: Rust formatting
        run: cargo fmt --all -- --check
      - name: Install source scanners
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2.87.31
        with:
          tool: cargo-deny,cargo-machete,typos-cli,shellcheck,actionlint@1.7.12
      - name: Source and supply-chain policy
        run: |
          typos
          cargo deny check
          cargo machete
          shellcheck --severity=warning scripts/*.sh scripts/release/*.sh .claude/hooks/*.sh hooks/*
          actionlint

For a reproducible race or timeout fix, use a regression or negative control that
fails for the original mechanism and passes with the repair. Confirm that the
intended case actually ran. Preserve existing coverage while investigating; any
temporary quarantine needs an explicit owner, reason, tracking issue and removal
condition under the existing gate policy.

## Reject incomplete discovery and generated-policy drift

Successful test execution requires successful, complete input discovery.
`scripts/ci/fuzz-targets.py` compares the discovered cargo-fuzz list with the actual
manifest-owned target inventory before running anything. Failed enumeration, an
empty list, duplicates, omissions or unknown targets fail the job, as do individual
target failures. Keep this assertion at the execution owner; shell loop command
substitution alone does not propagate discovery failure under `set -e`.

`scripts/ci/glib-migration.py` evaluates every resolved glib branch, rather than
treating a newer parallel branch as proof that an older stack was removed. Its
migration claim conservatively requires stable 0.20 or newer throughout; absent
glib and mixed old/new trees do not establish migration. The
[RustSec advisory](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2024-0429.html) owns the
security version ranges; the watcher retains native build/test and reviewed-PR
requirements before changing dependencies.

Generated native input probes share one accepted-key/extended-flag metadata owner
between WebDriver mapping and emitted C# policy. Regressions must check that every
emitted key is accepted with the correct flags and unsupported keys remain
rejected, rather than only matching the generated call text. Ownership checks and
real desktop acceptance remain separate from generator/compilation checks.

## Review the change and prevent renewed drift

Follow the existing validation stages; do not invent a parallel completion
process. For changes affecting CI behavior or recurring cost, include the
following in the normal [alignment review](maintenance-checklist.md#review-and-follow-up-procedure):

- The acceptance boundary and retained owner, including consumers affected by
  deletion, merging, selection or schedule changes.
- The measured bottleneck, comparable before/after scope and remaining unknowns;
  distinguish observed latency, resource cost and reliability.
- Executed validation and source identity, with inventory/provenance checks or
  regression controls appropriate to the changed mechanism.
- Remaining hosted, cross-platform, native or release evidence and the owner of
  any follow-up. Do not claim candidate acceptance from local or older results.

Workflow, runner and tool upgrades can change CLI semantics, report formats,
selectors and archive compatibility. Validate affected real tool invocations and
failure paths through the existing diagnostic owners; YAML parsing or unit mocks
alone do not establish the behavior of the installed tool.

Revisit timing and failure evidence when a gate becomes slower, starts rerunning,
gains another platform/dependency, or repeatedly exceeds its expected budget.
During existing maintenance reviews, inspect slow cases, duplicated setup,
shard imbalance, cache churn and abandoned temporary exceptions. Retire obsolete
work with its consumers and selectors rather than accumulating permanent layers.

Keep this review proportional: a documentation-only change needs applicable
formatting, links and structural checks, not a new build benchmark. Rules should
be enforceable through existing contracts and diagnostics where practical;
adding this guide does not create a scheduled job or another required check.

      MESH_ASAN_CARGO: ${{ needs.cohort.outputs.cargo }}
      MESH_ASAN_SHARDS_RESULT: ${{ needs.shards.result }}
      RUSTFLAGS: "-Zsanitizer=address"
      RUSTDOCFLAGS: "-Zsanitizer=address"
      ASAN_OPTIONS: "detect_leaks=1"
      RUST_TEST_THREADS: "1"
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - name: Download this attempt's ASan evidence
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: asan-${{ github.sha }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}-shard-*
          path: tmp/asan-union
      - name: Verify every actual shard and complete exact-source union
        run: node scripts/ci/asan.mjs verify tmp/asan-union
          !(github.event_name == 'pull_request' &&
            github.base_ref == 'dev' &&
            github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'dependabot[bot]')
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@303a32d7a59b442fa8d48b6a1cc6825c09c847a5 # v7.1.1
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          files: frontend/coverage/lcov.info
          name: frontend-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          fail_ci_if_error: true

  source:
    name: Source and supply-chain checks
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1
      # Source/policy scanners have identical inputs on each OS; run them once.
      # Gitleaks owns the full-history secret scan in its independent workflow.
      - name: Install Rust
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: rustfmt
      - name: Rust formatting
        run: cargo fmt --all -- --check
      - name: Install source scanners
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2.87.31
        with:
          tool: cargo-deny,cargo-machete,typos-cli,shellcheck,actionlint@1.7.12
      - name: Source and supply-chain policy
        run: |
          typos
          cargo deny check
          cargo machete
          shellcheck --severity=warning scripts/*.sh scripts/release/*.sh .claude/hooks/*.sh hooks/*
          actionlint

For a reproducible race or timeout fix, use a regression or negative control that
fails for the original mechanism and passes with the repair. Confirm that the
intended case actually ran. Preserve existing coverage while investigating; any
temporary quarantine needs an explicit owner, reason, tracking issue and removal
condition under the existing gate policy.

## Reject incomplete discovery and generated-policy drift

Successful test execution requires successful, complete input discovery.
`scripts/ci/fuzz-targets.py` compares the discovered cargo-fuzz list with the actual
manifest-owned target inventory before running anything. Failed enumeration, an
empty list, duplicates, omissions or unknown targets fail the job, as do individual
target failures. Keep this assertion at the execution owner; shell loop command
substitution alone does not propagate discovery failure under `set -e`.

`scripts/ci/glib-migration.py` evaluates every resolved glib branch, rather than
treating a newer parallel branch as proof that an older stack was removed. Its
migration claim conservatively requires stable 0.20 or newer throughout; absent
glib and mixed old/new trees do not establish migration. The
[RustSec advisory](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2024-0429.html) owns the
security version ranges; the watcher retains native build/test and reviewed-PR
requirements before changing dependencies.

Generated native input probes share one accepted-key/extended-flag metadata owner
between WebDriver mapping and emitted C# policy. Regressions must check that every
emitted key is accepted with the correct flags and unsupported keys remain
rejected, rather than only matching the generated call text. Ownership checks and
real desktop acceptance remain separate from generator/compilation checks.

## Review the change and prevent renewed drift

Follow the existing validation stages; do not invent a parallel completion
process. For changes affecting CI behavior or recurring cost, include the
following in the normal [alignment review](maintenance-checklist.md#review-and-follow-up-procedure):

- The acceptance boundary and retained owner, including consumers affected by
  deletion, merging, selection or schedule changes.
- The measured bottleneck, comparable before/after scope and remaining unknowns;
  distinguish observed latency, resource cost and reliability.
- Executed validation and source identity, with inventory/provenance checks or
  regression controls appropriate to the changed mechanism.
- Remaining hosted, cross-platform, native or release evidence and the owner of
  any follow-up. Do not claim candidate acceptance from local or older results.

Workflow, runner and tool upgrades can change CLI semantics, report formats,
selectors and archive compatibility. Validate affected real tool invocations and
failure paths through the existing diagnostic owners; YAML parsing or unit mocks
alone do not establish the behavior of the installed tool.

Revisit timing and failure evidence when a gate becomes slower, starts rerunning,
gains another platform/dependency, or repeatedly exceeds its expected budget.
During existing maintenance reviews, inspect slow cases, duplicated setup,
shard imbalance, cache churn and abandoned temporary exceptions. Retire obsolete
work with its consumers and selectors rather than accumulating permanent layers.

Keep this review proportional: a documentation-only change needs applicable
formatting, links and structural checks, not a new build benchmark. Rules should
be enforceable through existing contracts and diagnostics where practical;
adding this guide does not create a scheduled job or another required check.
"}

import { defineConfig, devices } from "@playwright/test";
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";

const worktreePort =
  5200 +
  (parseInt(
    createHash("sha256").update(process.cwd()).digest("hex").slice(0, 4),
    16,
  ) %
    1000);

  process.env.MESH_TALK_E2E_PORT ?? (process.env.CI ? 5173 : worktreePort),
);
// Keep browser navigation and server binding on the same address family.
const url = `http://127.0.0.1:${port}`;

// Browser E2E for the Mesh-Talk UI. Runs the Vite dev server + drives the real React app in
// headless Chromium with a mocked Tauri IPC layer (see e2e/tauri-mock.ts).
export default defineConfig({
  testDir: "./e2e",
  // A functional journey includes cold transforms, rendering and several
  // successful state assertions. Use the existing Windows/coverage watchdog
  // across platforms; individual assertion and product deadlines stay separate.
  timeout: 90_000,
  fullyParallel: true,
  forbidOnly: !!process.env.CI,
  retries: process.env.CI ? 1 : 0,
  // A single macOS worker avoids Vite asset decode retries and page-load
  // timeouts seen in the full suite with four concurrent browsers. CI already
  // uses one; Windows keeps its existing four-worker limit.
  workers:
    process.env.CI || process.platform === "darwin"
      ? 1
      : process.platform === "win32"
        ? 4
        : undefined,
  reporter: process.env.CI ? "list" : "html",
  snapshotPathTemplate: "e2e/{testFileName}-snapshots/{arg}{ext}",
  expect: {
    toHaveScreenshot: {

  },

  },
  projects: [{ name: "chromium", use: { ...devices["Desktop Chrome"] } }],
  webServer: {
    command: `npm run dev -- --host 127.0.0.1 --port ${port}`,
    env: { MESH_TALK_E2E: "1" },
    url,
    // Another worktree may already have Vite on this port. Reusing it can
    // silently test an older checkout and report a false pass or failure.
    reuseExistingServer: false,
    timeout: 120_000,

L80: # Continuous Integration
L81: ## Introduction【71†​】
L82: 
L83: Playwright tests can be executed in CI environments. We have created sample configurations for common CI providers.
L84: 
L85: 3 steps to get your tests running on CI:
L86: 
L87:   1. Ensure CI agent can run browsers: Use 【67†our Docker image】 in Linux agents or install your dependencies using the 【72†CLI】.
L88: 
L89:   2. Install Playwright:
L90: 
L91:     `
L92: 
L93:     # Install NPM packages
L94: 
L95:     npm ci
L96: 
L97:     # Install Playwright browsers and dependencies
L98: 
L99:     npx playwright install --with-deps
L100: 
L101:     `
L102:   3. Run your tests:
L103: 
L104:     `
L105: 
L106:     npx playwright test
L107: 
L108:     `
L109: ## Workers【73†​】
L110: 
L111: We recommend setting 【74†workers】 to "1" in CI environments to prioritize stability and reproducibility. Running tests sequentially ensures each test gets the full system resources, avoiding potential conflicts. However, if you have a powerful self-hosted CI system, you may enable 【18†parallel】 tests. For wider parallelization, consider 【75†sharding】 - distributing tests across multiple CI jobs.
L112: playwright.config.ts
L113: 
L114:     `
L115: 
L116:     import { defineConfig, devices } from '@playwright/test';
L117: 
L118:     export default defineConfig({
L119: 
L120:       // Opt out of parallel tests on CI.
L121: 
L122:       workers: process.env.CI ? 1 : undefined,
L123: 
L124:     });
L125: 
L126:     `
L127: ## Global timeout【76†​】
L128: 
L129: Always set a 【77†global timeout】 in CI. By default a test run has no upper bound, so a suite that hangs, or that slowly grows past the job limit of your CI provider, is killed by the runner mid-run and does not produce the test report.
L130: 
L131: With 【78†testConfig.globalTimeout】 set, Playwright stops the run itself.
L132: playwright.config.ts
L133: 
L134:     `
L135: 
L136:     import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';
L137: 
L138:     export default defineConfig({
L139: 
L140:       // Fail the run after an hour, so that the reporters still produce a report.
L141: 
L142:       globalTimeout: 60 * 60 * 1000,
L143: 
L144:     });
L145: 
L146:     `
L147: 
L148: The examples below therefore do not set a job-level timeout such as `timeout-minutes` in GitHub Actions. If you do add one, keep it comfortably above `globalTimeout`, so that Playwright always stops first.
L149: ## CI configurations【79†​】
L150: 
L151: The 【72†Command line tools】 can be used to install all operating system dependencies in CI.
L152: 
L153: ### GitHub Actions【80†​】
L154: #### On push/pull_request【81†​】
L155: 
L156: Tests will run on push or pull request on branches main/master. The 【82†workflow†docs.github.com】 will install all dependencies, install Playwright and then run the tests. It will also create the HTML report.

jobs:

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Apply the same reviewed-finding gate before merge and on main.

    env:

    permissions:
      security-events: write
      actions: read
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        language: [rust, javascript-typescript, actions]
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 22

      - name: Initialize CodeQL
        uses: github/codeql-action/init@9b3254085494b55a0f7c4c2b3d2d52cc712ce370 # codeql-bundle-v2.25.6 (v3)
        with:
          languages: ${{ matrix.language }}
          build-mode: none
          config-file: ./.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml

# Pull requests, merge candidates and main pushes verify the pinned runner's

  merge_group:

  push:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  runner-contract:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2.87.31
        with:
          tool: cargo-mutants@27.1.0,cargo-nextest@0.9.150
      - name: Verify pinned mutation runner behavior
        run: node --test scripts/diagnostics/mutants-workflow.test.mjs scripts/diagnostics/mutation-evidence.test.mjs scripts/release/run-mutants.test.mjs

  mutants:
    name: Workspace mutation sample (${{ matrix.worker }})
    needs: runner-contract
    if: github.event_name == 'schedule' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Cover setup plus 18 builds/suites (baseline and 17 mutants) at the
    # observed 130s build and bounded 360s suite budgets, without truncation.
    timeout-minutes: 180
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false # Keep other reports if one runner has a baseline/tool failure.
      matrix:
        worker: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    env:
      # rust-cache otherwise defaults this to 0, defeating per-mutant rebuild reuse.
      CARGO_INCREMENTAL: '1'
      MUTATION_WORKER: ${{ matrix.worker }}
      MUTATION_WORKERS: '4'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1 # Daily sampling does not need repository history

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0

# Keeping CI fast and reliable

Treat feedback time, reliability and resource use as maintained requirements.
Every feature, dependency and test can change CI cost, even without a workflow
edit. AI agents and contributors should preserve useful coverage while reducing
unnecessary work, and leave failures easier to reproduce and diagnose.

This guide owns CI maintenance decisions and regression prevention. It does not
introduce another workflow, command catalog or acceptance policy.

| Question                                            | Authoritative owner                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Which tests, commands and CI jobs apply?            | [Testing feedback loop](testing-feedback-loop.md), owning `validation.json` contracts and [workflow definitions](../.github/workflows/) |
| What evidence permits acceptance or release?        | [Quality gates](quality-gates.md) and [version and release lifecycle](updates.md#version-ownership-and-lifecycle)                       |
| Where does an implementation or shared rule belong? | [Module ownership](module-boundaries.md) and [script entry points](../scripts/README.md)                                                |
| Which consumers and documentation need updating?    | [Change alignment checklist](maintenance-checklist.md) and [documentation guidelines](DOCUMENTATION_GUIDELINES.md)                      |

Keep tool versions, matrix sizes, deadlines, cache keys and required-check names
in their existing executable owners. Keep run histories and investigation output
in ignored `tmp/` or PR/CI artifacts; durable decisions belong in the owning guide.

## Make the cost of a change explicit

Before adding a suite, fixture, dependency, platform or workflow, identify the
existing owner and the observable failure it must detect. Inspect the affected
plan and consumers through the [validation protocol](testing-feedback-loop.md#validation-stages-and-agent-responsibilities).
Answer four questions in the change when they are material:

- What requirement needs new evidence, and why is existing evidence insufficient?
- Which layer and platform can exercise that requirement faithfully?
- What recurring setup, compilation, execution and artifact cost will it add?
- Can an existing task, fixture or compatible output supply it without weakening
  assertions or introducing another owner for the same rule?

Extend the existing implementation first. Share policy and lifecycle rules where
their meaning is identical; keep feature-specific fixtures local. An abstraction
is useful when it removes duplicated decisions and has clear inputs, outputs and
failure behavior. Avoid both copied shell fragments and a generic CI framework
whose configuration is harder to review than the work it coordinates.

Do not make a full local suite the default for every edit. Use affected feedback
while developing, then complete the applicable boundary and candidate gates.
New tests still need independent assertions; matching the implementation or
increasing a test count does not establish useful coverage.

## Measure the bottleneck before choosing the optimization

Use the existing [timing reports](testing-feedback-loop.md#measure-feedback-before-tuning-capacity).
Distinguish time to actionable feedback, time until required checks complete,
runner execution minutes and failure/rerun frequency. A change can improve one
while worsening another. Runner minutes are not billing, and a green rerun does
not erase the first failure.

Compare equivalent source changes, test inventories, platforms, toolchains and
cache conditions. Retain cold and warm observations, sample size, cancellations
and missing data. P50/P95 from a small or mixed historical sample are descriptive;
one faster run is not a durable latency guarantee. Job creation-to-start time can
include dependencies, so do not label it all runner queue time or call the last
finishing job a proven critical path.

| Observed cost               | Investigate first                                                                 | Prefer before adding capacity                                                        |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Waiting to start            | Actual dependency graph, runner availability, obsolete candidates, matrix fan-out | Remove unnecessary dependencies and safely cancel superseded verification            |
| Installation or compilation | Step timing, dependency graph, cache restore/save cost and compatibility          | Remove repeated setup and reuse compatible outputs; inspect Cargo timings            |
| Long test execution         | Slow cases, fixture preparation, worker saturation, shard imbalance               | Fix expensive setup and balance measured work within resource limits                 |
| Intermittent failures       | First failure logs, traces, readiness, task lifetime and leaked resources         | Reproduce and repair the owning fixture, product behavior or infrastructure          |
| Evidence collection         | Archive sizes, compression, transfer, merge and upload time                       | Produce each required report once and separate optional presentation from acceptance |

[Cargo build timings](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/timings.html)
help distinguish compilation work from test execution. A test scheduler cannot
remove compilation cost. Include dependency installation, archive transfer and
reporting in the comparison; moving cost into another job is not removing it.

Set latency and resource expectations from representative observations and the
purpose of each gate. A job timeout is a safety bound, not a performance target.
Record material budget changes and their rationale in the owning configuration
and review, rather than inventing universal minute limits in this guide.

Stop an already failed candidate before starting another expensive compilation
partition. Linux/macOS native testing finishes all selected Host cases, then
admits the remaining complete workspace only if Host passed. Both partitions
still have to pass before reporting coverage; per-partition terminal result
collection, independent matrix jobs, default targets and zero retries remain
unchanged. The existing actual-tool coverage regression checks Host rejection,
remaining-partition rejection, successful coverage accumulation, timing pipelines
and report errors. Preserve partial backend evidence after a failure, while
requiring evidence on passing jobs; a producer skipped by an upstream failure
must not create a second missing-artifact error.

Keep complete tests distinct from duplicate instrumentation. macOS instruments
Host for its native desktop/updater branches, then runs every remaining default
workspace target with pinned Nextest without coverage instrumentation. Linux and
Windows retain full instrumented workspace coverage. This removes the separate
instrumented Core test build on Apple Silicon; it does not claim full macOS Core
line coverage. The actual-tool regression executes both workflow blocks, requires
all default targets and the Core execution marker, proves a clean macOS report
retains Host hits without a Core test cohort, and keeps both partition failures,
report failures, timing pipelines and process termination controls. All platform
assertions, doctests, zero retries and direct required checks remain unchanged.

A progressing serial test partition can exhaust its job watchdog without a hung
case. Windows reuses one sealed instrumented workspace archive across eight
independent serial consumers; every selected case still executes once with full
coverage, default targets, existing watchdogs and zero retries. Acceptance uses
those actual native checks directly. Do not add a second qualification workflow
or extend a job timeout to compensate for oversized units. Four extra setup and
archive transfers are a material cost; measure them alongside execution and runner
variation. The existing required-check owner retires old partition names only
after every current-source replacement passes with its bound app. Preserve strict
protection, unrelated checks and exact-source release acceptance together.

Treat a browser's total functional-case watchdog separately from its action,
assertion and product deadlines. A cold page, several successful state checks and
real interactions can cumulatively exhaust a short total bound without any one
operation failing. Full Chromium uses its existing Windows/coverage safety margin
on all hosts; portable execution retains its existing Windows allowance. Keep
state-based readiness, all assertions, explicit latency limits, zero retries and
first-failure traces. Do not erase a failed assertion by increasing its timeout.
The real-runner control derives both configured watchdogs, accelerates only their
duration, requires actual parked-case failure and subsequent-case execution, and
verifies descendant retirement before removing its fixture.

## Reuse compatible work with verifiable inputs

Prefer one producer for an expensive output when consumers need the same inputs
and artifact transfer is cheaper than rebuilding. Include the producer dependency
and its effect on parallelism in the measurement. Reuse compilation separately
from test execution: each required consumer still supplies its own assertions.
Keep production, coverage, sanitizer and mutation configurations distinct unless
their compatibility has been established.

Hosted Ubuntu Rust jobs prepare disk capacity before restoring Cargo outputs.
The [runner storage owner](../scripts/ci/runner-storage.mjs) reclaims only three
fixed unused SDK directories from disposable image contents and reports actual
free bytes before and after. Each heavy job uploads that small measurement before
cache expansion, so a later exhausted runner does not erase the preparation evidence.
It preserves the workspace, build caches and tools
used by compilation and analysis; local/self-hosted contexts and redirected paths
are not cleanup targets. Its real filesystem controls cover preservation and
idempotence. Inspect those measurements and cache expansion before responding
to disk exhaustion; a failed runner may be unable to upload its own logs.

A cache is an optional accelerator. A cold or evicted cache must still allow
correct execution. Measure restored bytes, restore/save time, useful hits and
eviction; a reported hit alone does not prove a faster build. Preserve the
existing trust boundaries and write policy. GitHub documents cache matching,
branch access and eviction in its [dependency caching reference](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/dependency-caching).

An artifact used as acceptance evidence has a stronger contract. Its consumer
must validate the actual tested head or merge source, workflow/run/attempt, platform and architecture,
relevant toolchain/features, expected inventory and content digests required by
the owning protocol. A matching filename, a successful download or a cache hit
is insufficient. Digests detect content changes; provenance establishes whether
those bytes belong to the intended candidate. Reject missing, stale, duplicate,
partial or incompatible inputs before merging evidence.

Keep these checks in the existing producer/consumer owner. Do not add a second
receipt format or evidence resolver. Exercise rejected-input cases when changing
that boundary, and preserve the documented rerun procedure for attempt-bound
artifacts. GitHub's download action reports a digest mismatch as a warning;
the evidence consumer must explicitly reject it. See [artifact validation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/tutorials/store-and-share-data#validating-artifacts)
for the platform behavior.

## Refactor coverage without losing its meaning

Two executions are redundant only when their requirement, inputs, platform and
evidence obligations are equivalent. A browser mock, real desktop process,
encrypted loopback exchange and physical network observation prove different
things. Keep the [platform evidence boundaries](platform-validation.md).

Before merging or deleting a check, map each assertion and downstream consumer
to its retained owner. Update affected selectors, fixtures, artifact consumers,
required checks and release consumers together where applicable. Validate the
replacement on the current candidate before the existing protected obligation
can be retired under the [quality gates](quality-gates.md). Eliminate redundant
aggregate jobs when direct checks provide the required enforcement; retain a
collector when it actually validates completeness or combines required evidence.

Selection and sharding need inventories, not just successful exit codes. Verify
that required cases are present, partitions are complete and disjoint where
intended, and expected platform-specific or ignored cases remain explicit.
Empty selections, skipped dependencies and incomplete collectors cannot stand in
for executed coverage. Moving Rust execution to another runner must also retain
separately owned doc-tests and integration/ignored-test obligations.

Use [same-source selection audits](testing-feedback-loop.md#qualify-affected-selection-alongside-full-gates)
before proposing narrower gates. Imports alone cannot reveal every runtime,
native or generated consumer. Moving a check from PRs to a schedule changes
detection latency and acceptance scope; describe and review that tradeoff rather
than calling it equivalent coverage delivered faster.

Workflow path filters and job conditions have different required-check behavior.
GitHub warns that a workflow skipped by path or branch filtering can leave its
required check pending; a skipped job can report success. A collector must still
run when a dependency fails and explicitly reject failed, cancelled, missing or
unexpectedly skipped required work. An `always()` condition schedules a collector;
it does not validate its dependencies. See [required-check troubleshooting](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/how-tos/merge-and-close-pull-requests/troubleshooting-required-status-checks).

The UI HTML collector follows the mandatory full-shard producers, independently
of the optional extended-browser jobs. If Health prevents desktop shards from
starting, their missing reports remain incomplete evidence. The collector checks
all four current-attempt shards per OS; fixing the upstream failure and rerunning
the selected producers supplies that evidence, rather than omitting those OSes.

## Bound parallelism and preserve isolation

on:

jobs:

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1

  mutants:
    name: Workspace mutation sample (${{ matrix.worker }})
    needs: runner-contract
    if: github.event_name == 'schedule' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Cover setup plus 18 builds/suites (baseline and 17 mutants) at the
    # observed 130s build and bounded 360s suite budgets, without truncation.
    timeout-minutes: 180
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false # Keep other reports if one runner has a baseline/tool failure.
      matrix:
        worker: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    env:
      # rust-cache otherwise defaults this to 0, defeating per-mutant rebuild reuse.
      CARGO_INCREMENTAL: '1'
      MUTATION_WORKER: ${{ matrix.worker }}
      MUTATION_WORKERS: '4'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1 # Daily sampling does not need repository history

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json

      - name: Install mutation test tools
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2.87.31
        with:
          tool: cargo-mutants@27.1.0,cargo-nextest@0.9.150

      - name: Select mutation sample
        id: selection
        working-directory: src-tauri
        run: node ../scripts/release/run-mutants.mjs --list-only

      - name: Prepare hosted Linux build storage
        id: runner_storage
        if: steps.selection.outputs.selected != '0' && runner.os == 'Linux'
        shell: bash
        run: sudo --preserve-env=GITHUB_ACTIONS,RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT,RUNNER_OS "$(command -v node)" scripts/ci/runner-storage.mjs --prepare | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/runner-storage.json"

      - name: Preserve runner storage measurements
        if: always() && steps.runner_storage.outcome == 'success'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: runner-storage-${{ github.job }}-${{ strategy.job-index || 0 }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/runner-storage.json
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14

      - name: Prepare Ubuntu archive source
        if: steps.selection.outputs.selected != '0'
        shell: bash
        run: sudo --preserve-env=GITHUB_ACTIONS,RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT,RUNNER_OS "$(command -v node)" scripts/ci/ubuntu-apt-source.mjs

      - name: Install Tauri system dependencies
        if: steps.selection.outputs.selected != '0'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libgtk-3-dev \
            libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf

      - name: Cache mutation build
        if: steps.selection.outputs.selected != '0'
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
          workspaces: '.'
          key: mutants

      - name: Build frontend
        if: steps.selection.outputs.selected != '0'
        working-directory: frontend
        run: |
          npm ci
          npm run build

      # The shared runner contract passed before these shards started.
      - name: Mutants (workspace sample)
        if: steps.selection.outputs.selected != '0'
        working-directory: src-tauri
        run: node ../scripts/release/run-mutants.mjs

      - name: Upload mutants report
        # A test-only/config-only diff can exit successfully without creating a report.
        if: always() && hashFiles('mutants.out/**') != ''
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: mutants-report-${{ matrix.worker }}
          path: mutants.out/
          if-no-files-found: error

  # Preserve the stable branch-protection check across matrix size changes.
  mutation-gate:
    name: mutants
    needs: [runner-contract, mutants]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: Require all mutation shards
        env:
          CONTRACTS: ${{ needs.runner-contract.result }}
          DEEP: ${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' }}
          SHARDS: ${{ needs.mutants.result }}
        run: |
          test "$CONTRACTS" = success
          if [ "$DEEP" = true ]; then
            test "$SHARDS" = success
          else
            test "$SHARDS" = skipped
          fi
',

    operator: 'match',
    diff: 'simple'
  }

import json,pathlib,collections,datetime,statistics,csv
p=pathlib.Path('tmp/ci-speed');rows=[]
def t(s):return datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s.replace('Z','+00:00')) if s else None
for r in json.loads((p/'runs-before.json').read_text()):
 for j in json.loads((p/f"jobs-{r['databaseId']}.json").read_text()).get('jobs',[]):
  if j['status']!='completed' or j['conclusion']=='skipped':continue
  steps=[]
  for x in j.get('steps',[]):
   a,b=t(x.get('started_at')),t(x.get('completed_at'))
   if a and b and b>=a:steps.append((x['name'],(b-a).total_seconds()))
  rows.append({'run':r['databaseId'],'workflow':r['workflowName'],'job':j['name'],'conclusion':j['conclusion'],'steps':steps,'dispatch':(t(j['started_at'])-t(j['created_at'])).total_seconds() if j.get('created_at') and j.get('started_at') else None})
(p/'baseline-completed-steps.json').write_text(json.dumps(rows,indent=2));print('completed executed jobs',len(rows));print(collections.Counter(r['conclusion'] for r in rows));print('dispatch median',statistics.median(r['dispatch'] for r in rows if r['dispatch'] is not None))

text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > tmp/ci-speed/pr-body.md <<'EOF'
ASan's four serial partitions have an uneven execution tail (one successful baseline: approximately 28/24/15/20 minutes). Split the complete inventory across eight serial Nextest runners, preserving instrumentation, case deadlines, zero retries, clean/error controls, exact-source receipts and the required exhaustive-union collector.

Superseded PR verification also remained queued behind unconditional collectors after producer cancellation. Collector jobs now remain eligible after upstream failure but release cancelled workflows. Every main push has a unique concurrency group so pending commits cannot replace one another; PR and merge candidates still cancel older runs. Health downloads pinned actionlint instead of compiling it with Go.

Extend docs/ci-maintenance.md with measurement-first guidance for agents: phase accounting, cache budgets, prebuilt tools, repeat builds, runner admission, required-check-safe docs selection and actual hosted follow-up. No test inventory, required check name, platform assertion, release gate or coverage obligation is removed.

Validation: actionlint; 83 focused regressions including real pinned Nextest eight-partition execution and failure/omission/duplication controls; structural standards, repository hygiene and whitespace checks. Frontend builds in the original checkout: 722ms then 537ms. The broader local affected selector rejects a Windows-only test's intentional skip on macOS; that command is not a pass. Hosted Windows evidence remains required. Hosted before/after measurement is in progress.

Docs-only workflow filtering is deliberately withheld: protected checks include external app-bound CodeQL and Codecov results, and release consumers require complete main verification. A path filter alone would strand required checks; no synthetic success or protection weakening is introduced.
EOF

import json,pathlib,collections,datetime,statistics,csv
p=pathlib.Path('tmp/ci-speed');rows=[]
def t(s):return datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s.replace('Z','+00:00')) if s else None
for r in json.loads((p/'runs-before.json').read_text()):
 for j in json.loads((p/f"jobs-{r['databaseId']}.json").read_text()).get('jobs',[]):
  if j['status']!='completed' or j['conclusion']=='skipped':continue
  steps=[]
  for x in j.get('steps',[]):
   a,b=t(x.get('started_at')),t(x.get('completed_at'))
   if a and b and b>=a:steps.append((x['name'],(b-a).total_seconds()))
  rows.append({'run':r['databaseId'],'workflow':r['workflowName'],'job':j['name'],'conclusion':j['conclusion'],'steps':steps,'dispatch':(t(j['started_at'])-t(j['created_at'])).total_seconds() if j.get('created_at') and j.get('started_at') else None})
(p/'baseline-completed-steps.json').write_text(json.dumps(rows,indent=2));print('completed executed jobs',len(rows));print(collections.Counter(r['conclusion'] for r in rows));print('dispatch median',statistics.median(r['dispatch'] for r in rows if r['dispatch'] is not None))
PY

cat > tmp/ci-speed/pr-body.md <<'EOF'
ASan's four serial partitions have an uneven execution tail (one successful baseline: approximately 28/24/15/20 minutes). Split the complete inventory across eight serial Nextest runners, preserving instrumentation, case deadlines, zero retries, clean/error controls, exact-source receipts and the required exhaustive-union collector.

Superseded PR verification also remained queued behind unconditional collectors after producer cancellation. Collector jobs now remain eligible after upstream failure but release cancelled workflows. Every main push has a unique concurrency group so pending commits cannot replace one another; PR and merge candidates still cancel older runs. Health downloads pinned actionlint instead of compiling it with Go.

Extend docs/ci-maintenance.md with measurement-first guidance for agents: phase accounting, cache budgets, prebuilt tools, repeat builds, runner admission, required-check-safe docs selection and actual hosted follow-up. No test inventory, required check name, platform assertion, release gate or coverage obligation is removed.

Validation: actionlint; 83 focused regressions including real pinned Nextest eight-partition execution and failure/omission/duplication controls; structural standards, repository hygiene and whitespace checks. Frontend builds in the original checkout: 722ms then 537ms. The broader local affected selector rejects a Windows-only test's intentional skip on macOS; that command is not a pass. Hosted Windows evidence remains required. Hosted before/after measurement is in progress.

Docs-only workflow filtering is deliberately withheld: protected checks include external app-bound CodeQL and Codecov results, and release consumers require complete main verification. A path filter alone would strand required checks; no synthetic success or protection weakening is introduced.
EOF
gh pr edit 338 --body-file tmp/ci-speed/pr-body.md

name: Sanitizers

# Memory-safety / leak guardrail: runs the pure-Rust core test suite under
# AddressSanitizer (ASan, which embeds LeakSanitizer) so a genuine leak or
# use-after-free in the protocol core fails the build.
#
# Scope: ONLY `mesh-talk-core --lib` (the UI-free core). The Tauri app links
# GTK/WebKit C libraries whose internals trip ASan with false positives we can't
# fix from here, so the app is deliberately excluded.
#
# Run on PRs targeting main so branch protection can require this memory-safety
# check before merge. Run again on main so the README badge reflects the merged
# code; keep the weekly run to catch toolchain and dependency drift.
# ASan needs the nightly toolchain + `-Z build-std` (a full std rebuild).
on:
  merge_group:
    types: [checks_requested]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  push:
    branches: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 6 * * 1" # Mondays 06:00 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:

# Read-only: just checks out and runs the test suite under the sanitizer.
permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}-${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.run_id || 'candidate' }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'merge_group' }}

jobs:
  cohort:
    name: Resolve ASan nightly cohort
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      toolchain: ${{ steps.cohort.outputs.toolchain }}
      rustc: ${{ steps.cohort.outputs.rustc }}
      cargo: ${{ steps.cohort.outputs.cargo }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - name: Resolve installed nightly manifest
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@nightly
        with:
          components: rust-src
      - name: Publish exact installed nightly cohort
        id: cohort
        run: node scripts/ci/asan.mjs cohort

  shards:
    name: ASan core shard (${{ matrix.shard }}/8)
    needs: cohort
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]
    env:
      MESH_ASAN_TOOLCHAIN: ${{ needs.cohort.outputs.toolchain }}
      MESH_ASAN_RUSTC: ${{ needs.cohort.outputs.rustc }}
      MESH_ASAN_CARGO: ${{ needs.cohort.outputs.cargo }}
      RUSTFLAGS: "-Zsanitizer=address"
      RUSTDOCFLAGS: "-Zsanitizer=address"
      ASAN_OPTIONS: "detect_leaks=1"
      # Keep production case budgets and one instrumented test per runner.

item.aggregated_output:
name: Sanitizers

# Memory-safety / leak guardrail: runs the pure-Rust core test suite under
# AddressSanitizer (ASan, which embeds LeakSanitizer) so a genuine leak or
# use-after-free in the protocol core fails the build.
#
# Scope: ONLY `mesh-talk-core --lib` (the UI-free core). The Tauri app links
# GTK/WebKit C libraries whose internals trip ASan with false positives we can't
# fix from here, so the app is deliberately excluded.
#
# Run on PRs targeting main so branch protection can require this memory-safety
# check before merge. Run again on main so the README badge reflects the merged
# code; keep the weekly run to catch toolchain and dependency drift.
# ASan needs the nightly toolchain + `-Z build-std` (a full std rebuild).
on:
  merge_group:
    types: [checks_requested]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  push:
    branches: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 6 * * 1" # Mondays 06:00 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:

# Read-only: just checks out and runs the test suite under the sanitizer.
permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  RUSTFLAGS: "-Zsanitizer=address"
  RUSTDOCFLAGS: "-Zsanitizer=address"
  ASAN_OPTIONS: "detect_leaks=1"
  RUST_TEST_THREADS: "1"

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}-${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.run_id || 'candidate' }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'merge_group' }}

jobs:
  cohort:
    name: Build ASan test archive
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      toolchain: ${{ steps.cohort.outputs.toolchain }}

---
name: dispatching-parallel-agents
description: Use when facing 2+ independent tasks that can be worked on without shared state or sequential dependencies
---

# Dispatching Parallel Agents

## Overview

You delegate tasks to specialized agents with isolated context. By precisely crafting their instructions and context, you ensure they stay focused and succeed at their task. They should never inherit your session's context or history — you construct exactly what they need. This also preserves your own context for coordination work.

When you have multiple unrelated failures (different test files, different subsystems, different bugs), investigating them sequentially wastes time. Each investigation is independent and can happen in parallel.

**Core principle:** Dispatch one agent per independent problem domain. Let them work concurrently.

## When to Use

```dot
digraph when_to_use {
    "Multiple failures?" [shape=diamond];
    "Are they independent?" [shape=diamond];
    "Single agent investigates all" [shape=box];
    "One agent per problem domain" [shape=box];
    "Can they work in parallel?" [shape=diamond];
    "Sequential agents" [shape=box];
    "Parallel dispatch" [shape=box];

    "Multiple failures?" -> "Are they independent?" [label="yes"];
    "Are they independent?" -> "Single agent investigates all" [label="no - related"];
    "Are they independent?" -> "Can they work in parallel?" [label="yes"];
    "Can they work in parallel?" -> "Parallel dispatch" [label="yes"];
    "Can they work in parallel?" -> "Sequential agents" [label="no - shared state"];
}
```

**Use when:**
- 3+ test files failing with different root causes
- Multiple subsystems broken independently
- Each problem can be understood without context from others
- No shared state between investigations

**Don't use when:**
- Failures are related (fix one might fix others)
- Need to understand full system state
- Agents would interfere with each other

## The Pattern

### 1. Identify Independent Domains

Group failures by what's broken:
- File A tests: Tool approval flow
- File B tests: Batch completion behavior
- File C tests: Abort functionality

Each domain is independent - fixing tool approval doesn't affect abort tests.

### 2. Create Focused Agent Tasks

First instrument TCP/Noise accept, handshake start/end, and runtime scheduling delay to distinguish local worker starvation from Windows networking delay. import subprocess,json,concurrent.futures,collections,pathlib
runs=json.loads(subprocess.check_output(['gh','run','list','--limit','100','--json','databaseId,status,workflowName,headBranch'],text=True));runs=[r for r in runs if r['status']!='completed']
def get(r):return r,json.loads(subprocess.check_output(['gh','api',f"repos/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/actions/runs/{r['databaseId']}/jobs?per_page=100"],text=True))
with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=6) as ex:data=list(ex.map(get,runs))
pathlib.Path('tmp/ci-speed/final-queue-snapshot.json').write_text(json.dumps(data,indent=2));counts=collections.Counter()
for r,j in data:
 for x in j['jobs']:
  if x['status']=='in_progress':counts[r['headBranch']]+=1
print(dict(counts))
PY
